tips.title: The Two-Cut Method with GodHand SPN-120 Nippers
tips.text: GodHand SPN-120 Ultimate Nippers have razor-sharp edges that leave almost no stress mark, but they are fragile and will chip if used on thick gates. Use the two-cut method: first cut the gate 2mm from the part with cheaper nippers (Tamiya 74123), then make the final flush cut with the GodHand. Never twist or pull the part off — always cut straight through. This works especially well on delicate Eduard photo-etch frets and Clear Prop Models canopy parts.

tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Scribing Tool
tips.text: RB Productions Scribing Tool creates clean, precise panel lines without smearing. Hold the tool at a 30° angle to the surface, apply light pressure, and drag it across the plastic. For deeper lines, use the tool with a light coat of Tamiya Plastic Cement applied with a brush. This technique is ideal for fine detailing on Arma Hobby or ICM kits, ensuring crisp lines that won’t smear during painting.

tips.title: Photo-etch Bending Jig for Eduard Frets
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch parts require precise bending to avoid cracking. Use a 1.5mm thick bending jig (such as Clear Prop Models' 200mm jig) and apply gentle pressure. Heat the part with a heat gun (200°C) for 5 seconds before bending, then cool with a hair dryer. This technique ensures crisp bends for ICM or Arma Hobby detail parts.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Airbrush
tips.text: Iwata airbrush needles get clogged with paint residue. Use a 0.3mm diameter brass needle cleaner (Iwata part #004-1038) to clear blockages. Soak the cleaner in isopropyl alcohol for 10 minutes, then gently twist it through the needle. Clean daily after use, and replace the needle every 50 hours of use for optimal spray quality.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape adheres well to clean plastic but can peel if painted over. Use it for large areas, then cover with Kabuki tape (1.5mm thick) for fine lines. Apply Kabuki tape with a squeegee (Tamiya 74120) to avoid bubbles. After painting, peel the tape off immediately to prevent paint transfer. This method works best on ICM or Hobby Boss kits for sharp edges and clean lines.
